yearConvention: Forecast years are NHL season ending years; frontend contract years are start years and must add one at the boundary.
caveats: Expected delivered contribution includes participation and workload; not isolated intrinsic ability.
Age curves use returning-player changes; a separate NHL-return model includes exits but cannot eliminate all selection bias.
Peer selection uses origin histories; unknown follow-up never supplies a zero or replacement peer. Development and calibration remain subject to selection and historical-data limitations.
Peer influence is learned from earlier completed forecast targets. Insufficient or unhelpful comparable evidence falls back to the broader position path.
Long-range estimates extrapolate individual and broad development curves, not independently validated distant-season models.
Unknown positive-GP outcomes are excluded, never zero. Current incomplete seasons and salaries never enter fitting.
Retrospective, previously inspected source reconstructions are not untouched prospective confirmation.
Residual ranges are horizon-specific historical errors, not guaranteed future coverage or contract confidence intervals.
Peer trajectories personalize shape rather than guaranteeing larger improvement for every above-average young player.
First-step peer transitions are omitted to avoid counting initial regression twice; subsequent curve evidence is conditional on measured NHL returners.

Relative effective peer count is discounted by absolute similarity. Same-age median and phase grouping are origin-known; group definitions and model variants were inspected during diagnostic research.
Peer blend weights use older OOF forecasts with completed targets only; overlapping player/origin/horizon rows are dependent. No untouched prospective confirmation is claimed.
Paired historical effect versus v2 is mixed: small defenseman improvement and small forward/goalie deterioration at pooled horizons2-5. No overall predictive superiority is claimed.
Full-term means retain all numeric remaining years; distant years remain extrapolations.
